newsitem.title: UK: B. Midland year profits soar up 45 pct.
newsitem.headline: B. Midland year profits soar up 45 pct.

text.p: European regional airline British Midland Airways announced on Wednesday that it made a pre-tax profit of 7.1 million pounds last year, cruising up from 4.9 million in 1995, on sales up 7.8 percent at 478.2 million pounds.
The airline said average loadings rose 1.7 percentage points to 63.2 percent with 5.6 million passengers carried on its scheduled services last year, up 300,000 on 1995.

Midland, which ranks as London Heathrow's second largest operator behind British Airways, with 1,500 flights a week, said it had benefitted from expanding its widespread network of code-sharing agreements with other airlines.
The carrier added two more code-share deals last year to give it separate deals with a total of 17 international carriers at Heathrow.
And it was also close to agreeing a new operational deal with German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG on routes between Germany and Britain.
"Talks are at an advanced stage between the two airlines to expand services to other destinations in the UK and Germany," Midland said in a statement.

But chairman and controlling shareholder Sir Michael Bishop dismissed recent speculation that his airline would shortly join the Star Alliance grouping which was launched last week and includes Lufthansa, United Airlines and Midland's 40 percent shareholder Scandinavian Airline Systems. Bishop said it was too early to choose between the various multilateral alliances being developed to create global reach, such as British Airways' proposed deal with American Airlines.

"I think it's important to say that you will notice we were not a part of the announcement of the Star Alliance last week," he told reporters. Instead Midland would continue to pursue bilateral partnerships, he said.
"We are not giving any commitment to any multilateral consortium," he said.
